findings.text: follow-on: DEFECT introduced by this run — the code-scan retry backoff moved inside the progress-callback guard. At base 3fb07d05 the line `await _sleep_unless_stopped(state, backoff)` sat at function-body indentation (workers.py:278), so it ran on every reachable-error retry. In commit 40ed29859 it became `await reachability._sleep_unless_stopped(state, backoff)` indented one level deeper, inside the `if on_progress:` block that follows the `on_progress(...)` call (workers.py:238). The intended change was to call the same helper through its new module; the incidental re-indent changed control flow. Consequence: when scan_worker is driven with on_progress=None (its default, and what the engine passes whenever on_scan_progress is None -- both production WorkerSpecs forward on_progress only when the callback is not None, engine.py:160), the host-reachable retry loop no longer sleeps at all, so a repeatedly-failing remote scan becomes a no-delay busy loop that re-issues the batched SSH call as fast as it fails, exactly the failure state section 63 exists to bound. REPRODUCED at head: a probe driving scan_worker with on_progress=None and a reachable CalledProcessError(1) (the same harness the file's own run_retrying_scan builds) records `remote_calls: 5` and `backoff_waits: []` (reviewer-backoff-probe.log); the identical drive against a scratch checkout of base 3fb07d05 records `backoff_waits: [2, 4, 8, 16]` (reviewer-backoff-probe-base.log). Uncovered by the run's own tests: tests/discovery/test_code_scan_failures.py::test_script_failure_still_stops_after_the_retry_limit asserts only claim state and remote.call_count == 5, never the backoff waits, so 12/12 still pass with the backoff entirely absent.

follow-on: the shared module keeps `_sleep_unless_stopped` private and workers.py reaches into it as `reachability._sleep_unless_stopped` (workers.py:238) while importing `host_unreachable`/`wait_for_reachable_host` by name. A module that two subsystems now depend on is better served by a public `sleep_unless_stopped` than by a leading-underscore name read from outside the module; the private access is the only reason the call site was rewritten rather than left as a bare call. Cosmetic, not a behavior defect.
